subject: Mythology
title: Geasa: Sacred Taboos and Magical Oaths
description: A quick, practical guide to Geasa: Sacred Taboos and Magical Oaths.

hook.text: Celtic heroes were bound by geasa — sacred taboos that gave them power but destroyed them if they ever broke one.

buildup.text: Cu Chulainn was forbidden from eating dog meat and from refusing hospitality. Both were impossible to keep forever.

discovery.text: A geis could be placed by druids, gods, or powerful women. Refusing one brought shame worse than death.

twist.text: Enemies often exploited geasa by creating situations where the hero had to choose between two conflicting taboos.

climax.text: Cu Chulainn's death came when enemies forced him to break his geasa one by one, draining his supernatural power.

punchline.text: The same rules that made heroes invincible also guaranteed their doom.

quiz.question: What were geasa in Celtic mythology?
options: Magical weapons given to heroes by the gods
Sacred taboos that gave power but destroyed heroes if broken
Protective spells cast by druids before battle
